parsed.why: No facility ban, but no statewide accommodations or hate-crime coverage, birth certificates retain original sex, custody denies transition care; undercount killings figure unusable. Roughly parent-level, slightly offset by limited protections.

Top-tier state: statewide public-accommodations protection, hate-crime enhancements, panic-defense repeal, X markers, shield laws — genuine visitor-facing positives — but national document, entry and custody regimes still bind the traveler.

Most protective record: facilities access protected, hate-crime conviction, courts ordering care restored, prison consent decree, chosen-name rules. National document and custody regimes remain, and pending ballot measures create pressure, but local record is strongest.

Facility law by birth sex in all schools/colleges, DMV restricting markers to matching M/F, no statewide nondiscrimination statute, second-tier 'worst policies' ranking. Below parent average despite no enforcement mechanism attached to the facility law.

Protective tier: accommodations law covering hotels and shops, mandatory gender-neutral single-occupancy toilets, shield law aiding visitors from ban states, hate-crime coverage, X markers. National document and entry regimes still govern discovery.
